basis: Dermal mucin deposition causes skin induration; associated diabetes, infections and malignancies are separate conditions.
Mature teratoma arising in the central nervous system.
Infantile interstitial lung disease; inflammation alone does not establish an immune-mediated mechanism.
Localized dermal mucinous nodules; no evidence of thyroid disease or systemic organ damage.
Congenital structural abnormality of the coronary arteries.
Adenocarcinoma originating in extrahepatic bile ducts, which belong to the hepatic axis.
Definition specifies a malignant CNS glial tumour; anomalous child entries do not establish other organ involvement.
Glyoxylate metabolic disorder defined by renal oxalate disease; nephrolithiasis, nephrocalcinosis and abnormal renal physiology occur in 80-99%.
ARL6-related rod-cone retinal degeneration; other ciliopathy manifestations cannot be inferred from the gene.
Inflammation of a vein; infection or an autoimmune mechanism is not inherent to this umbrella concept.
Neoplasm located in the endocardium of the heart.
Inherited iron overload; hepatic injury is common in clinical disease, often >50%; characteristic arthropathy affects roughly 30-50%; cardiac injury is less common.
Infection directly affecting skin; unrelated sites in individual child entries do not apply across the group.
Skin/nail dystrophy, marrow failure and oral leukoplakia define dyskeratosis congenita; pulmonary fibrosis 3/6. Hepatic fibrosis 2/6 and osteoporosis 3/6 omitted under cap.
Germ cell tumour arising in the CNS; endocrine injury depends on tumour location and is not established across the group.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; ptosis 2/2, strabismus/myopia 1/2 support ocular dysfunction; scoliosis, kyphosis and contracture 1/2 support skeletal involvement; small sample.
Inherited skeletal muscle dystrophy; respiratory failure reflects muscle weakness, not direct lung damage. Cardiac dysfunction 1/4 is below threshold.
Acute gonococcal infection of the bladder; bladder belongs to the renal axis.
Renal resistance to vasopressin causes defective water conservation and hypernatremia in 80-99%; neurological sequelae are uncommon.
Malignant neoplasm involving the lung hilum.
Definition describes heterotopic bone formation in deep soft tissues, usually after trauma; inflammatory naming does not establish autoimmunity.
Relative polycythemia from reduced plasma volume; associated hypertension and vascular risks do not establish additional direct organ damage.
Arthropathy affects joints; progeria-associated features elsewhere cannot be assigned to this joint-specific concept.
Cancer arising in the short bones of the upper limb.
Primary skin-based T-cell lymphoma: cutaneous origin, lymphoid blood-cell neoplasm and lymphoma mechanism; extracutaneous spread is not typical.
